name: Gooseberry Fool
description: Historical recipe from Common Sense in the Household (1871). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: Méringue of whites, and 3 tablespoonfuls sugar
ingredients.originalText: Méringue of whites, and 3 tablespoonfuls sugar

instructions.text: Stew the gooseberries in just water enough to cover them
When soft and broken, rub them through a sieve to remove the skins
While still hot beat in the butter, sugar, and the whipped yolks of the eggs
Pile in a glass dish, or in small glasses, and heap upon the top a méringue of the whipped whites and sugar

source.author: Marion Harland
source.originalInstructions:
1. Stew the gooseberries in just water enough to cover them
2. When soft and broken, rub them through a sieve to remove the skins
3. While still hot beat in the butter, sugar, and the whipped yolks of the eggs
4. Pile in a glass dish, or in small glasses, and heap upon the top a méringue of the whipped whites and sugar
